anomalies.observed: In this build the ATO solenoid valve is switched by T6, an AO3400A (SOT-23, 30 V / 5.7 A) low-side MOSFET, driven from the pre-driver T3 (BT3904) through R50 (100 Ω); the AON6407 (8-DFN) in the same build is used as T5 in the 24 V input path instead of driving the valve.
anomalies.expected: The ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch should be the AON6407 (8-DFN) power MOSFET, per the specification: "T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch" (spec §2), with the matching r2 device set "T1/T4 BT3904 ×2, T2 IRLR2905, T3 AON6407, T5 AO3400A ×1" (spec §5).

evidence.quote: "T6  AO3400A" in the ATO Valve driver of the MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS block (sheet 1/1, tile 3), gate resistor "R50 100Ω", pre-driver "T3 BT3904"
"T5  AON6407" placed in the 24 V input path of the POWER TRAIN block, together with D2 (12 V) and C40 (10 µF) (sheet 1/1, tile 1)
T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch. Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: The ATO solenoid is driven by a much smaller device than intended (SOT-23 ~5.7 A / ~28 mΩ instead of the 8-DFN AON6407), reducing current and thermal margin on the 24 V valve output, while the higher-current AON6407 is spent in the 24 V input path. If the valve current or inrush exceeds the AO3400A's capability the ATO fill function can overheat or fail.

parsed.summary: The build's 24 V switch devices are swapped relative to the intended design: the ATO solenoid valve is switched by an AO3400A (SOT-23) instead of the specified AON6407 (8-DFN), which appears in the 24 V input path instead. The rest of what could be read (TPS62933/AZ1117 power train, ADM3260 isolated pH/EC channels with the RTD left on the main bus, 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-ups, 110 mΩ TMC2209 sense resistors and charge-pump networks, DNP environmental sensors/LiDAR) matches the specification.
